params.name: Ring composition
params.instruction: Arrange corresponding subjects or episodes in reverse order around a central turn, so the second half answers the first.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Place paired units in reverse order around one central turn; the number of pairs may vary.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"A"},{"position":2,"name":"B"},{"position":3,"name":"C"},{"position":4,"name":"Central turn"},{"position":5,"name":"C′"},{"position":6,"name":"B′"},{"position":7,"name":"A′"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Beowulf"},{"work":"Iliad","creator":"Homer"},{"work":"Odyssey","creator":"Homer"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"John D. Niles, Ring Composition and the Structure of Beowulf","url":"https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/pmla/article/abs/ring-composition-and-the-structure-of-beowulf/B36957736B90889A1C2F0261D7592A88","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Frame narrative
params.instruction: Open an enclosing situation in which one or more interior narratives are told, then return to the enclosing situation.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Outer situation"},{"position":2,"name":"Occasion for telling"},{"position":3,"name":"Interior narrative or narratives"},{"position":4,"name":"Return to the outer situation"},{"position":5,"name":"Outer closure"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Decameron"},{"work":"The Canterbury Tales"},{"work":"One Thousand and One Nights"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"The Cambridge Introduction to Narrative, Borders of Narrative","url":"https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/cambridge-introduction-to-narrative/borders-of-narrative/0B5E1442AD2222F266D3E0D900E8508F","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Epistolary form
params.instruction: Construct the work from letters and other documents whose dates, authors, recipients, omissions, and contradictions determine disclosure order.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Documents establish correspondents and situation"},{"position":2,"name":"Exchanges accumulate partial accounts"},{"position":3,"name":"Gaps or contradictions alter understanding"},{"position":4,"name":"Surviving correspondence supplies or withholds closure"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Pamela","creator":"Samuel Richardson"},{"work":"Clarissa","creator":"Samuel Richardson"},{"work":"Dracula","creator":"Bram Stoker"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"Oregon State University, What is an Epistolary Novel?","url":"https://liberalarts.oregonstate.edu/wlf/what-epistolary-novel","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Interlace narrative
params.instruction: Alternate among concurrent narrative lines, suspend a line at a charged point, and resume it after visiting the others until the lines meet or answer one another.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Open two or more concurrent lines, alternate among them while earlier lines remain unresolved, then bring the lines into relation.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Establish line A"},{"position":2,"name":"Switch to line B while A remains unresolved"},{"position":3,"name":"Continue through further lines or returns"},{"position":4,"name":"Resume earlier lines"},{"position":5,"name":"Converge or close the lines in relation"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Lancelot-Grail Cycle"},{"work":"Orlando Furioso","creator":"Ludovico Ariosto"},{"work":"The Lord of the Rings","creator":"J. R. R. Tolkien"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"Richard West, The Interlace Structure of The Lord of the Rings","url":"https://commons.und.edu/theses/6711/","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Reverse chronology
params.instruction: Present the principal events from latest to earliest, so causes arrive after their effects.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Final event or condition"},{"position":2,"name":"Immediate predecessor"},{"position":3,"name":"Successively earlier causes"},{"position":4,"name":"Earliest event or origin"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Betrayal","creator":"Harold Pinter"},{"work":"Memento","creator":"Christopher Nolan"},{"work":"Irréversible","creator":"Gaspar Noé"}]

params.name: Circular narrative
params.instruction: Return at the end to the opening situation, event, or wording, with the intervening work changing how the beginning is understood.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Opening situation"},{"position":2,"name":"Departure or expansion"},{"position":3,"name":"Consequences"},{"position":4,"name":"Return to the opening"},{"position":5,"name":"Reinterpretation or repetition"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Finnegans Wake","creator":"James Joyce"},{"work":"Decline and Fall","creator":"Evelyn Waugh"},{"work":"Of Mice and Men","creator":"John Steinbeck"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"Stephanie E. Katz, Here We Go 'Round in Circles","url":"https://etheses.bham.ac.uk/id/eprint/13395/","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Linked-story cycle
params.aliases: ["Short-story cycle","short-story sequence","composite novel","linked stories","novel in stories"]
params.instruction: Arrange stories that can be read independently so recurring people, places, or consequences also make a larger work.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Order self-contained stories so shared elements revise or extend the larger work, then close through accumulation rather than one continuous plot resolution.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Self-contained story"},{"position":2,"name":"Later story with a shared element"},{"position":3,"name":"Further independent stories revise or extend the whole"},{"position":4,"name":"Cumulative closure"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Winesburg, Ohio","creator":"Sherwood Anderson"},{"work":"Dubliners","creator":"James Joyce"},{"work":"The Things They Carried","creator":"Tim O'Brien"}]

params.name: Cumulative narrative
params.instruction: Repeat a stable passage while adding one person, object, or deed at every recurrence, sometimes undoing the series in reverse.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Repeat a stable passage with one addition at each recurrence; after maximum accumulation, the series may unwind in reverse or release abruptly.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Base incident"},{"position":2,"name":"First repetition plus addition"},{"position":3,"name":"Successive repetitions plus additions"},{"position":4,"name":"Maximum accumulation"},{"position":5,"name":"Optional reverse unwinding or abrupt release"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Gingerbread Man"},{"work":"The House That Jack Built"},{"work":"The Old Woman and Her Pig"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"A Companion to the Fairy Tale, Catch If You Can: The Cumulative Tale","url":"https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/companion-to-the-fairy-tale/catch-if-you-can-the-cumulative-tale/DD2204C4C9F3E9E3B7641D191FD8551C","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Multiperspectival narrative
params.instruction: Present an event or subject through several materially different viewpoints whose agreement or conflict determines what the reader can know.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Present at least two distinct accounts, then let their agreement, conflict, or unresolved difference determine the work's knowledge.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Account from viewpoint A"},{"position":2,"name":"Account from viewpoint B"},{"position":3,"name":"Further accounts or returns"},{"position":4,"name":"Comparison and revision"},{"position":5,"name":"Reconciliation or unresolved contradiction"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Moonstone","creator":"Wilkie Collins"},{"work":"The Waves","creator":"Virginia Woolf"},{"work":"My Name Is Red","creator":"Orhan Pamuk"}]

params.name: Diary form
params.instruction: Build the work from dated entries written close to the narrated events, so chronology, gaps, and the diarist's limited knowledge control disclosure.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Order dated entries near their narrated events and use the sequence, gaps, and limited knowledge to control disclosure.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Initial dated entry and situation"},{"position":2,"name":"Periodic entries after events"},{"position":3,"name":"Omissions or revisions across gaps"},{"position":4,"name":"Last entry or editorial closure"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Diary of a Nobody","creator":"George and Weedon Grossmith"},{"work":"The Yellow Wallpaper","creator":"Charlotte Perkins Gilman"},{"work":"Flowers for Algernon","creator":"Daniel Keyes"}]

params.name: Hypertext narrative
params.instruction: Divide the work into text units connected by links, leaving reading order partly to the reader while controlling which units can follow which.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Connect text units as a directed network that constrains, but does not fully determine, the reader's path.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Entry node"},{"position":2,"name":"Reader-selected link"},{"position":3,"name":"Reachable node"},{"position":4,"name":"Further traversal"},{"position":5,"name":"Exit or open cessation"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"afternoon, a story","creator":"Michael Joyce"},{"work":"Victory Garden","creator":"Stuart Moulthrop"},{"work":"Patchwork Girl","creator":"Shelley Jackson"}]

params.name: Branching narrative
params.instruction: Place consequential choices at decision points so a reader or player selects one of several authored continuations and endings.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Branch the authored path at consequential choices; later paths may remain separate, rejoin, or loop before reaching distinct endings.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Common opening"},{"position":2,"name":"Choice point"},{"position":3,"name":"Branch"},{"position":4,"name":"Later choice or convergence"},{"position":5,"name":"Branch-specific ending"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Cave of Time","creator":"Edward Packard"},{"work":"80 Days","creator":"Inkle"},{"work":"Black Mirror: Bandersnatch"}]

params.name: Anachronic modular narrative
params.instruction: Arrange substantial narrative units from different times without giving one chronology stable priority until late in the work, if at all.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Order substantial modules from different times without a controlling chronology, then align them late or leave their relation partly unresolved.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Temporal module A"},{"position":2,"name":"Module from another time"},{"position":3,"name":"Further reordered modules"},{"position":4,"name":"Late causal alignment or residual uncertainty"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Pulp Fiction"},{"work":"21 Grams"},{"work":"Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"Matthew Campora on Allan Cameron's Modular Narratives in Contemporary Cinema","url":"https://www.sensesofcinema.com/2010/book-reviews/modular-narratives-in-contemporary-cinema-by-allan-cameron/","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Forking-path narrative
params.instruction: Repeat a common situation with a changed decision or circumstance, then follow mutually exclusive outcomes as parts of the authored work.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Establish a common situation and divergence, follow two or more mutually exclusive outcome paths, returning to the common situation or divergence before each additional path, then compare the paths or select a final outcome.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Common situation"},{"position":2,"name":"Divergence"},{"position":3,"name":"Outcome A"},{"position":4,"name":"Reset or return to divergence"},{"position":5,"name":"Outcome B"},{"position":6,"name":"Comparison or final selected outcome"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Groundhog Day"},{"work":"Run Lola Run"},{"work":"Sliding Doors"}]

params.name: Sustained allegory
params.instruction: Compose a literal narrative whose people, places, and events maintain a second coherent sequence of meaning across the complete work.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Establish literal terms"},{"position":2,"name":"Establish corresponding figurative terms"},{"position":3,"name":"Develop both sequences together"},{"position":4,"name":"Resolve the literal sequence and figurative argument"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Faerie Queene","creator":"Edmund Spenser"},{"work":"The Pilgrim's Progress","creator":"John Bunyan"},{"work":"Animal Farm","creator":"George Orwell"}]

params.name: Aristotelian complication and denouement
params.instruction: Develop one causally unified plot through complication, then turn through recognition or reversal into denouement.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Move from the beginning through complication, include recognition, reversal, or both when present, then proceed through the denouement to the end.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Beginning"},{"position":2,"name":"Complication"},{"position":3,"name":"Reversal or recognition when present"},{"position":4,"name":"Denouement"},{"position":5,"name":"End"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Oedipus Rex","creator":"Sophocles"},{"work":"Iphigenia in Tauris","creator":"Euripides"},{"work":"Odyssey","creator":"Homer"}]

params.name: Freytag's five-part dramatic structure
params.instruction: Raise dramatic force from introduction through a central climax, then reduce it through return and catastrophe.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Introduction"},{"position":2,"name":"Rise"},{"position":3,"name":"Climax"},{"position":4,"name":"Return or fall"},{"position":5,"name":"Catastrophe"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Hamlet","creator":"William Shakespeare"},{"work":"Macbeth","creator":"William Shakespeare"},{"work":"Julius Caesar","creator":"William Shakespeare"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"Gustav Freytag, Technique of the Drama, chapter 2","url":"https://www.briantriber.com/WritingSamples/Freytag_Drama/Freytag_11_Ch2_P2.html","handling":"public_domain"}]

params.name: Field three-act structure
params.instruction: Divide a screenplay into setup, prolonged confrontation, and resolution, with a decisive plot point changing direction at each division.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Setup"},{"position":2,"name":"First plot point"},{"position":3,"name":"Confrontation"},{"position":4,"name":"Second plot point"},{"position":5,"name":"Resolution"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Chinatown"},{"work":"Network"},{"work":"Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid"}]

params.name: Thompson four-part structure
params.instruction: Divide a feature into setup, Complicating Action, sustained development, and climax, with an optional short epilogue.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Use four required parts in order, then optionally add a short epilogue.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Setup"},{"position":2,"name":"Complicating Action"},{"position":3,"name":"Development"},{"position":4,"name":"Climax"},{"position":5,"name":"Optional epilogue"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Back to the Future"},{"work":"The Silence of the Lambs"},{"work":"Groundhog Day"}]

params.name: Eight-sequence structure
params.instruction: Build a feature from successive short dramatic units, commonly eight, with every unit posing and resolving a local question while advancing the larger work.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Use successive short dramatic units, commonly eight. Each unit poses and resolves a local question, and the last resolves the principal dramatic question.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Sequence 1"},{"position":2,"name":"Sequence 2"},{"position":3,"name":"Sequence 3"},{"position":4,"name":"Sequence 4"},{"position":5,"name":"Sequence 5"},{"position":6,"name":"Sequence 6"},{"position":7,"name":"Sequence 7"},{"position":8,"name":"Sequence 8 resolves the principal question"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Toy Story"},{"work":"North by Northwest"},{"work":"The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring"}]

params.name: Yorke five-act structure
params.aliases: ["Into the Woods five-act model","symmetrical five-act structure"]
params.instruction: Arrange five acts around a central acquisition or revelation, then make the later acts test and revise the earlier movement toward change.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Initial condition and awakening"},{"position":2,"name":"Commitment"},{"position":3,"name":"Midpoint acquisition or revelation"},{"position":4,"name":"Consequences and crisis"},{"position":5,"name":"Changed resolution"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"The Godfather"},{"work":"Hamlet","creator":"William Shakespeare"},{"work":"Breaking Bad"}]

params.name: Kishōtenketsu
params.instruction: Introduce and develop a subject, bring in a third-part turn that changes its relation, then connect all parts in the conclusion.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Ki, introduction"},{"position":2,"name":"Shō, development"},{"position":3,"name":"Ten, turn or disjunction"},{"position":4,"name":"Ketsu, connection and conclusion"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Final Fantasy VII"},{"work":"The Key","creator":"Jun'ichirō Tanizaki"},{"work":"The Castle of Cagliostro","creator":"Hayao Miyazaki"}]

params.name: Jo-ha-kyū
params.instruction: Begin slowly, expand and accelerate through the central development, then conclude rapidly, with the same pacing relation available at nested scales.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Jo, slow introduction"},{"position":2,"name":"Ha, development, break, and acceleration"},{"position":3,"name":"Kyū, rapid conclusion"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Takasago"},{"work":"Atsumori"},{"work":"Hagoromo"}]

params.name: Pancha-sandhi
params.instruction: Develop a dramatic seed through five junctures from its first indication to the attainment that completes it.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Mukha, opening"},{"position":2,"name":"Pratimukha, progression"},{"position":3,"name":"Garbha, development"},{"position":4,"name":"Vimarśa or avamarśa, pause, obstruction, or reversal"},{"position":5,"name":"Nirvāhaṇa, conclusion"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Abhijñānaśākuntalam","creator":"Kālidāsa"},{"work":"Mṛcchakaṭika","creator":"Śūdraka"},{"work":"Uttararāmacarita","creator":"Bhavabhūti"}]

params.name: Abstract episodic structure
params.instruction: Arrange causally weak episodes by a non-narrative ordering system such as a count, alphabet, catalogue, or repeated formal rule.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Choose a count, alphabet, catalogue, or repeated formal rule and order causally weak episodes by it until the series completes or breaks.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Establish the ordering rule"},{"position":2,"name":"Present successive episodes according to it"},{"position":3,"name":"Complete or break the series"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Drowning by Numbers","creator":"Peter Greenaway"},{"work":"A Zed & Two Noughts","creator":"Peter Greenaway"}]

params.name: Narrative anthology
params.instruction: Place apparently separate narratives in the same fictional world, then let shared places, encounters, or consequences disclose their relation.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Develop separate strands in a shared world, then disclose their relation through setting, crossover, or consequence.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Strand A"},{"position":2,"name":"Separate strand B"},{"position":3,"name":"Further strands"},{"position":4,"name":"Crossovers or shared setting"},{"position":5,"name":"Collective or parallel closure"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Dekalog","creator":"Krzysztof Kieślowski"},{"work":"Mystery Train","creator":"Jim Jarmusch"},{"work":"Short Cuts","creator":"Robert Altman"}]

params.name: Split-screen narrative
params.instruction: Divide the visual field into two or more frames so concurrent or earlier events remain visible together and their timing or contrast creates the work's organization.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Maintain at least two visible frames, coordinate their timelines, and use attention, sound, and intersections to organize the work.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Establish frames"},{"position":2,"name":"Align their timelines"},{"position":3,"name":"Vary attention or sound priority"},{"position":4,"name":"Create intersections"},{"position":5,"name":"Conclude together or release the division"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Timecode"},{"work":"Conversations with Other Women"},{"work":"Pretend"}]

params.name: Alternating parallel narrative
params.instruction: Alternate between two complete narrative lines whose comparison, causal relation, or eventual meeting supplies the larger design.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Line A"},{"position":2,"name":"Line B"},{"position":3,"name":"Alternating development"},{"position":4,"name":"Correspondence or convergence"},{"position":5,"name":"Paired or common resolution"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Mrs Dalloway","creator":"Virginia Woolf"},{"work":"The Hours","creator":"Michael Cunningham"},{"work":"All the Light We Cannot See","creator":"Anthony Doerr"}]
params.sources: [{"title":"ERIC, Reading and Writing in the Middle Grades, parallel-narrative unit","url":"https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED472279.pdf","handling":"cited_and_paraphrased"}]

params.name: Nested narrative
params.instruction: Descend through two or more narrative levels, then return through those levels so information from an inner account changes the containing account.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Descend through at least two narrative levels, then return through them in reverse order so the inner account changes its container.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Outer level"},{"position":2,"name":"Embedded level"},{"position":3,"name":"Optional deeper level"},{"position":4,"name":"Innermost account"},{"position":5,"name":"Return through the levels in reverse order"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Frankenstein","creator":"Mary Shelley"},{"work":"Wuthering Heights","creator":"Emily Brontë"},{"work":"The Manuscript Found in Saragossa","creator":"Jan Potocki"}]

params.name: In medias res
params.instruction: Open after the underlying events have begun and make the rest of the work disclose the omitted causes through backward reference or embedded recounting.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Mid-course opening"},{"position":2,"name":"Immediate present development"},{"position":3,"name":"Disclosure of earlier causes"},{"position":4,"name":"Convergence of past and present"},{"position":5,"name":"Continuation to the end"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Iliad","creator":"Homer"},{"work":"Odyssey","creator":"Homer"},{"work":"Paradise Lost","creator":"John Milton"}]

params.name: Mise en abyme
params.instruction: Insert a smaller representation of the containing work that comments on, predicts, or revises the reader's understanding of that complete work.
params.movements: {"kind":"fixed","parts":[{"position":1,"name":"Containing narrative"},{"position":2,"name":"Inset representation"},{"position":3,"name":"Recognized correspondence"},{"position":4,"name":"Altered reading of the containing narrative"},{"position":5,"name":"Outer resolution"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"Hamlet","creator":"William Shakespeare"},{"work":"The Counterfeiters","creator":"André Gide"},{"work":"Inception","creator":"Christopher Nolan"}]

params.name: Braided essay
params.instruction: Alternate recurring nonfiction strands without requiring chronological or causal continuity, and let their accumulating relation supply the conclusion.
params.movements: {"kind":"rule","rule":"Alternate two or more recurring nonfiction strands and let their accumulating relation, rather than chronology or causation, supply the close.","example":[{"position":1,"name":"Strand A"},{"position":2,"name":"Strand B"},{"position":3,"name":"Optional strand C"},{"position":4,"name":"Repeated alternation with shorter or more intense sections"},{"position":5,"name":"Convergence or relational close"}]}
params.exemplars: [{"work":"A Braided Heart","creator":"Brenda Miller"},{"work":"Time and Distance Overcome","creator":"Eula Biss"},{"work":"The Fourth State of Matter","creator":"Jo Ann Beard"}]
